prompt.context: Our client, Lights Camera Action Entertainment (LCA), is a major movie production house. After a disappointing summer filled with numerous box office flops, the CEO of LCA has approached us to decide which movie the company should release next.
prompt.question: Which movie should LCA release next in order to achieve a hit, defined as a movie with ROI greater than 50%?

clarifying_info.a: LCA is a production house in the US but releases movies across major global markets. They have a distribution network of domestic and international theatres and get a share of ticket sales.
They've been in the business for the past decade and have a good mix of movies across different genres.
The COVID-19 pandemic has wreaked havoc on the movie industry.

clarifying_info.q: What is the financial situation of the company?
clarifying_info.a: Even though the company did not have a major hit over summer, the company has ample cash reserves from investors. The board has indicated, however, that they expect a hit soon, or else the CEO will be looking for a new job.

clarifying_info.q: Do they have any financial target?
clarifying_info.a: The board is concerned about ROI after the recent flops and has classified a hit as a movie that has an ROI > 50%.

exhibits.title: LCA Movie Options
exhibits.shows: A table listing four candidate movies with their genre, total production costs (millions $), and forecasted theatre attendance (%)

exhibits.title: Global Movie Industry Statistics — Anticipated Theater Demand By Genre
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing anticipated domestic and international theatre counts by genre (Comedy, Drama, Action, Animated) for an average 30-day theatre run

exhibits.title: Global Theatres Statistics
exhibits.shows: A table showing LCA's revenue per ticket, number of shows per day, and number of seats per show for international and domestic theatre types

framework: Revenues: number of theaters at release, ticket price, fill rate per theater, merchandise licensing, sequel potential
Costs: actors, sets, special effects, advertising, editing, sound, production design
Non-financial internal factors: sequel of prior hit, saturation of series, expertise in a genre, exclusive actor deals, adaptation from popular novels
Non-financial external factors: macroeconomic trends, actor popularity, genre reach, trending themes/pop culture, clash with other release dates, competition from streaming (Netflix, etc.)

questions.prompt: Which of the four genres/movies is the most profitable option for LCA? Calculate monthly revenue, profit, and ROI for each option.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize this is a profitability case. Strong candidates will push to get granular on revenue drivers (theaters * seats * fill rate * ticket price). They should ask for theatre and ticket data (Exhibit 3) if not provided. Smart candidates may eliminate Life at Ivy (highest cost, lowest attendance) from Exhibit 1 and eliminate Paws at Pav (fewest theatres) from Exhibit 2 before calculating, saving time. After calculations, Comedy (Project Huntington) wins on ROI (212%) even though Action generates higher absolute profit.

math.setup: Monthly revenue per theatre type = LCA revenue/ticket * shows/day * seats/show * 30 days. Total revenue for a genre = fill_rate * domestic_theatres * domestic_monthly_earnings + fill_rate * international_theatres * international_monthly_earnings. ROI = (Revenue - Cost) / Cost.
math.answer: Comedy (Project Huntington) has the highest ROI at 212%, followed by Action at 170%, Animation at 20%, and Drama at -28%. Although Action generates the highest absolute profit ($127.5M), Comedy delivers the best ROI, which is the board's stated criterion for a hit (ROI > 50%).

brainstorming.prompt: Other than the profitability analysis, what are the other strategic decisions that LCA should consider for the success of their next movie?

categories.name: Content and Marketing
ideas: Use the marketing budget to drive awareness and buzz for the movie through appropriate channels
Cast the right actors, production and direction, and sound crew
Align the movie theme/story with ongoing social and pop culture and macroeconomic trends

categories.name: Release Timing
ideas: Choose strategic release dates to coincide with holidays or popular events (e.g., romcom during Valentine's weekend, holiday films over Christmas)
Avoid clashes with other popular movies or large sporting events during release

categories.name: Monetization
ideas: Merchandise sales tied to the movie category (e.g., water tumblers, limited edition gadgets, t-shirts)
Potential for sequels based on movie popularity
Release the movie on streaming platforms such as Netflix and Hulu and obtain television streaming rights
Consider the impact of initial reviews on theatre fill rates for subsequent weeks

recommendation: Even though Action (Case Wars) generates higher absolute profit ($127.5M vs $106M), Comedy delivers a superior ROI of 212% vs 170%, directly meeting the board's criterion of ROI > 50%; Comedy also has a lower production cost ($50M) reducing downside risk
risks: Critics and popular reviews could negatively affect theatre fill rates in subsequent weeks
Audience preferences may shift, and theatres may change their genre mix
COVID-19 pandemic impact on theatre attendance could reduce fill rates below forecasted levels
next_steps: Invest in releasing Project Huntington, choosing an appropriate release date (e.g., aligned with a relevant holiday or pop culture moment)
Launch a targeted advertising campaign leveraging appropriate marketing channels
Analyze scope of future revenues from sequels or merchandise licensing partnerships
